Found during the work on PR #2927 and PR #3010 (#2919, #2973).

The STEP reader gives an item that no representation lists (no unit context) the default units: 1 mm per length unit and the radian per angle unit. After PR #2927, a millimetre-only file keeps such items, because the length default is the file's own unit.

The angle default is not checked. A file can state a plane angle unit in degrees in its only context and also hold an item with no context. The reader then reads the angles of that item in radians. The imported geometry is wrong, and the import gives no warning.

`main` has the same gap today. PR #2927 does not make it worse.

Work:
1. Apply the rule of the length unit to the angle unit: keep an item with no context only when every stated angle unit is the default (the radian), or no angle unit is stated.
2. Otherwise, refuse the item by name, as the length-unit refusal does.
3. Add a pinning test: a degree-only file with an unlisted item that uses an angle (a cone or a conical surface).

body:
Research only. No code comes from this issue (AGENTS.md "needs-research").

**Why.** Many hobby router owners (WorkBee, Shapeoko, X-Carve, Onefinity, Laguna and Grizzly routers) use Vectric's **VCarve** or Delft Spline's **DeskProto**. Both are known for getting a first part cut quickly. One such user, MisterMaker on Discord (WorkBee with an Estlcam controller, #3038), never uses 3D CAM because building a 3D part from a 2D sketch is "too much of a hassle". Asked by the user (mkinney), 2026-11-20.

**Clean-room boundary** (same as #3045). The vendors' public material (feature pages, published manuals and tutorials, public videos) is used only as a checklist of which workflows and features hobby users expect. Never copied: wording, UI labels, parameter names, screen layouts, icons or dialog flows. Behaviour is specced from machining knowledge and our own design.

**Open questions**
1. **Typical first job.** What steps does a typical hobby job take in each tool: job and material setup, importing a 2D or 3D source, choosing toolpaths, the tool database, preview, saving G-code? Where does CamCraft take more steps or more knowledge today? Compare on 3 to 5 typical jobs: a sign, a V-carved name, an inlay, a 3D relief from an STL or image, a pocket and profile with tabs.
2. **Missing features.** Which hobby-router features do we lack or only half-cover? Candidates: V-carving (#1443), inlays, text and fonts, relief from an image or heightmap, tabs and bridges, ramps and lead-ins, "cut out" profiling, nesting (see #2395), toolpath templates, simple job wizards, machine and post pickers for common routers, simulated preview in wood colours.
3. **Defaults and presets.** Which defaults and starter presets would let a new router user get a safe first cut with no CAM knowledge? Router tool libraries (end mills, V-bits, ball noses) with conservative feeds, machine presets, material thickness and zero-point prompts.
4. **What not to copy.** Which of their simplifications would break our "never gouge, refuse with a reason" rules, and how do we keep the safety and still stay simple?

A user who puts `camcraft-cli` on their PATH with a symlink (the usual way on macOS, where the binary is inside `CamCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/`) cannot post. MCP clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor) are set up with such a path.

| Started as | `process <project> -o out.nc` |
|---|---|
| `/Applications/CamCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/camcraft-cli` | rc 0, posted |
| a symlink to that file, in another folder | rc 1 |
| a copy of that file, in another folder | rc 1 |

```
ERROR camcraft_app::posting::files: shipped posts file tormach.cps: no posts folder found - the program needs its assets/posts directory beside the executable (looked in: <folder of the symlink>/assets/posts)

```

- A symlinked `camcraft-cli` finds the shipped posts (resolve the executable path with `std::fs::canonicalize` before the lookup), with a test.

body: ## What happens When an operation's Geometry has a picked face, the viewport draws the face outline as a thick violet stroke with a dark halo (`pick_ink` -> `pick_highlight_mesh::paint_selected`, #1505). Seen from a low angle, the stroke becomes a wedge: a second violet line separates from the outline and grows wider toward the edge of the viewport, until it reaches the edge. - The wedge shows in all themes (dark and light). - The line width and the anti-aliasing do not change it. It shows at 1 pt with anti-aliasing Off on the #2958 branch. ## Where it comes from These three builds were compared at the same low view of the same project (a picked top face, Face operation): | Build | Result | |---|---| | v0.24.0 release | No wedge. Some halo segments disappear at some angles and zoom levels (see below). | | `main` at acd5b02d3 | Wedge | | `main` + #2989 | Wedge | The pick highlight was rewritten after v0.24.0, in PR #2256 (#2201: cached geometry, one batched mesh of stroke paths). Thus the wedge is a regression of that change. - A probe of `egui::epaint::Tessellator` with a thin, acute closed path does not extend past its points. Thus a miter at a sharp corner is probably not the cause. - A likely cause is the screen projection of the world points. `push_screen_polyline_runs` projects each point by itself (`interact::project_uv`). - A point behind the eye (`w <= 1e-6`) is dropped, and the run continues to the next point that projects. - A point just in front of the near plane projects to a very large screen position. - Neither case clips the segment at the near plane, so a run can connect two points that are not neighbours on the outline, or go to a point far off the screen. ## Related: the halo that disappears (also in v0.24.0) In v0.24.0, at some angles and zoom levels, parts of the thick stroke disappear, and only the thin depth-tested overlay line stays. The cause is the same projection: a segment with an end behind the eye is dropped. This is older than the wedge. ## Expected The thick pick outline follows the picked edges at each angle and zoom. A segment that crosses the near plane is clipped at the near plane. It is not dropped, and it is not connected to another part of the outline. ## Done means - Each segment of the selected-pick and hover highlights is clipped at the near plane in clip space before it is projected. - A run never joins two points that are not neighbours on the outline. - A test with a picked rectangle seen from a low angle, with a corner behind the eye: - Each stroke vertex stays within the stroke width of the projected (clipped) outline. - No segment of the outline is missing. Found during the test of #2958 (PR #2989). #2989 does not change this code. Proposed labels: `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`

body:
Found during #2865. Related catalog work: #2392.

Base: upstream/main `58cb641ca`.

Use original closed meshes. Revolve each listed `(radius, Z)` meridian about Z with 48 angular segments.
Use `assets/machines/lathe.mch` and the `Fanuc Lathe` post.
Import the blank as stock with `set_stock {from_model: ...}`.
Set `set_raw_stock_only {on: true}`. Keep all verification checks active.

## What happens

Multi-Pass Turning roughs a neck in a short axial window.
Generation succeeds. Verification blocks the post:

```text
finish envelope near move 235: 0.0073 mm gouge, 2.2543 mm rest
```

## Reproduce

The finished meridian is:

```text
(0,0), (8,0), (10,2), (10,12), (9,12), (9,40), (8,60), (0,60)
```

The blank meridian is:

```text
(0,0), (10,0), (10,12), (9,12), (9,40), (8,60), (0,60)
```

Use `TN-1600-0R8` and the finished model as source.
Create these operations in order:

1. Chamfering: fixed clearance 70, top 2, bottom 0, angle 45 degrees.
2. Taper Turning: fixed clearance 70, top 60, bottom 40, diameters 18 and 16.
3. Multi-Pass Turning: fixed clearance 70, top 20, bottom 2.

For Multi-Pass Turning, use stepdown 0.5, stock allowance 0.25 and three passes.
Use tolerance 0.05, feed 120 and plunge feed 40 for all three operations.
Generate, then call `verify`.

The first two operations have separate completion warnings.
The multi-pass operation also has the quoted independent warning.

The original bushing attempt had more outside features and a blind bore.
It produced the same 2.2543 mm rest value near move 387.

## Expected result

The operation must judge its promised window and 0.25 mm allowance.
Other model regions must not add rest to that promise.

## Passing comparison

This simpler finished meridian verifies and posts:

```text
(0,0), (8,0), (10,2), (10,12), (9,12), (9,60), (0,60)
```

Use a diameter 20 blank over Z0..60.
Create Chamfering over Z0..2, then Multi-Pass Turning over the full Z0..60.
Keep tolerance 0.05, stepdown 0.5, allowance 0.25, three passes and 48 angular segments.

This comparison changes the model and operation window.
It does not identify which change avoids the refusal.

What happens (v0.24.0, macOS universal release build, `camcraft-cli 0.24.0`):

A user's real two-setup Tormach 770MX project (8 operations, one tool) regenerates and verifies clean - `gate.ok: true`, no problems, no findings, nothing held - but the post is refused:

```
camcraft-cli process sc_logo.camproj -o sc_logo-v0.24.0.nc
camcraft-cli: post: post engine: post script: post output line limit exceeded
exit 1
```

Posting one file per operation (MCP `set_post_options {"per_op": true}` then `post`) is refused the same way, at one operation:

```
post: S1 Notch adaptive + terrace finish: post engine: post script: post output line limit exceeded
```

That operation is a 3D Pocket (offset rings, stepdown 0.15 mm over ~15.5 mm depth, stepover 2.032 mm, T 1/4 in flat) that generates 105,592 moves - one more file than the cap allows. The cap is `MAX_OUTPUT_LINES = 100_000` in `crates/post/src/post/js.rs` (the runaway-script guard of `js_host.rs` PRELUDE `_emitLine`). The other ops are 13,791 + 39,904 + 10,443 + smaller moves, so the whole program is ~170k lines.

Why it is wrong: the guard exists to stop a looping script, but it also refuses a legitimate, verified program, so the user cannot make the part from CamCraft at all (per-op output does not get round it). A Tormach PathPilot control runs files of this size. The message also gives no number and (in `process`) no operation, so the user cannot tell what to change.

Workaround: raise the op's stepdown or split it into two Z ranges (changes the finish the user designed).

Expected:
- A program whose line count follows from its toolpath posts; the guard scales with the input (e.g. a bound derived from the number of moves/operations), or is far higher than any real toolpath, and still stops a runaway script.
- If a limit still refuses, the refusal names the limit, the line count reached and the operation.

Evidence: the user's project (local, not in the repo); a synthetic fixture with a 3D Pocket of >100k moves reproduces it. Found while re-posting the user's showcase parts on v0.24.0 (user goal "the two parts"); before v0.24.0 this project was refused earlier by #1749, so the cap was never reached.

Done means: a verified program over 100,000 lines (pinned by a test with a >100k-move operation) posts through the Tormach post whole and per operation; a real runaway script is still refused, and that refusal names the limit and the operation.

body:
The maintainer decided on 2026-11-20: widen the verdict tolerance for a model that opens at reduced accuracy. This issue holds that work. Part of #2976.

## What happens

PR #2994 (issue #2976) opens a STEP file whose edges lie as far off their surfaces as the tolerance that the file states. The model is meshed at a coarser tolerance (up to 0.02 mm) and gets the reduced-fidelity flag and a note.

A program on that model cannot be posted. The fidelity law (#864) permits a verdict only while the excess of the mesh tolerance over the import chord is inside `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm). The measured case: the chord is 0.02 mm, the import chord is 0.005 mm, so the excess is 0.015 mm. The law then has no verdict tolerance, and each operation is refused by name unless its stock to leave covers the excess. A finishing operation thus cannot post. The command `VouchModelFidelity` does not apply, because the chord is a measured value.

The file is legal and it opens. The user has a workaround only for roughing (stock to leave). Thus the priority is `P3`.

## What is wanted

- The verdict tolerance of such a model is the mesh deviation of the model itself, with a hard upper limit (for example 0.02 mm). The limit is a constant that no file can raise.
- The posted program says so: a comment in the program header names the model and the tolerance that the checks used. The UI shows the same fact as a note in plain English.
- The vouch command is not the mechanism for this.

## Safety

The gouge check must stay conservative in the direction that matters: the tool must not cut deeper than the real surface permits.

- The mesh can stand inside or outside the real surface by its deviation. The check must not count that deviation in favour of the tool. State the rule for each direction (a cut into the part, and material left on the part), and why a gouge of the real surface larger than the limit still blocks the post.
- The stock simulation, the keep law, the rest material and the collision checks each read the verdict tolerance. List each reader and what changes in it.
- A model at full fidelity keeps today's law, with no change of any verdict.

## Done when

- A test with a model at reduced accuracy (our own fixture, mesh deviation just under the limit) pins that a finishing operation posts, and that the program header has the note.
- A test just over the limit pins the refusal by name.
- A test pins that a real gouge deeper than the verdict tolerance still blocks the post on such a model.
- Each full-fidelity pin of the fidelity law stays green and unchanged.
- The decision file names the rule, the limit and what the user loses.

## Order

The code needs PR #2994 on `main`. The research does not.

Part of #2976. Refs #2994, #864

body:
Found by the read-only second review of PR #2927. The finding comes from a read of the code. No run proves it.

## What can happen

A STEP file can use the short entity names of ISO 10303-21. The short name of `PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT` is `PLANUN` (public ISO short-name registry, `https://standards.iso.org/iso/10303/tech/short_names/short-names.txt`, line 1554). The solidcore p21 parser does not map this name, and PR #2927 does not add it.

A file that states its angle unit as degrees with the short name then has no angle unit that the reader can find. The reader uses radians. An angle that the file gives in degrees, for example the semi-angle of a cone, is then read as radians. The surface has the wrong shape, and no refusal or note tells the user.

Wrong geometry is wrong output for each toolpath and each gouge check. Thus the priority is `P1` until a test shows the correct angle or a refusal.

## Where

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs`: the rename step that PR #2927 adds for `GUAC` and `SUNT`, and the unit read after it.
- The same registry gives `GC` for `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`. It is not mapped. That changes the tolerance only: check it in the same work.

## What is expected

- The reader reads the angle unit of a short-name file, or
- a file that has an angle unit that the reader cannot resolve is refused by name. An angle is never read in a unit that the file does not state.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with short names and a cone whose angle is in degrees, is in `testdata/models/`.
- A test imports it. The cone has the correct angle (checked by a size that depends on the angle), or the import is refused by name.

Refs #2919, #2927

Found while fixing #2901.

**What happens.** After a tool change the machine does not know its X/Y. The first traverse of an operation can cross any point of the setup. #2901 adds the first-traverse law (`sim::verify::first_traverse_low`). The law applies only to the 2D milling, 3D milling and vertical hole kinds on a mill without a rotary axis, upright or 3+2.

These operations have no such law:
- operations in a setup with a rotary axis (4th-axis wrap and the rotary kinds);
- the multi-axis kinds (continuous 5-axis, swarf, flow);
- the cross drill (radial holes).

Before #2901, the opening rapid started at the WCS origin. The rapid law judged that line by accident. The machine does not travel that line, so the old check did not protect these kinds either. The rapid laws and the simulation judge only the moves that the path contains.

**Expected.** Each of these kinds has a stated first-traverse law, or a named refusal, for its own clearance surface (for example the clearance radius about the A axis, against the stock and the chuck and tailstock).

**Evidence.** `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` (`answers`) excludes these kinds. The decision is in `docs/decisions/2901-first-traverse-law.md`.

Done means: for each excluded kind, a test shows that a clearance surface inside the stock or a fixture holds the post by name, or the decision file records why the kind cannot have that collision.

body: ## Problem The viewport draws toolpaths, height-plane rectangles, region outlines and the other overlay lines as `wgpu` `LineList` primitives (`crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`, `overlay_pipeline`). A `wgpu` line is always 1 hardware pixel wide. The viewport targets use `sample_count: 1`, thus the lines also have no anti-aliasing. The result: - The lines are thin and jagged. On a display with 150 % scale, they are thinner again. - The feed colour (green) has low contrast against the grey stock. It is hard to see the paths and the direction chevrons. - The WCS triad does not have this problem. egui draws it again over the GPU image with a 3 px anti-aliased stroke (#195, `GIZMO_STROKE_PX`). Thus the triad is much easier to see than the toolpath. ## Trial A trial on a local branch (not pushed) rendered `examples/first-part.camproj` through the real viewport pipelines (`gpu_render` test harness). The operation Face1 is open, thus its height planes show. **1. Close view. Before: today. After: 1.5 px wide lines, MSAA 4x, depth offset.** **2. Full view. 1.5 px stays clear when the camera is far. 2 px and 2.5 px made the dense paths into one solid area, thus 1.5 px is the default.** **3. Depth offset. Without it, a wide line that lies on a face is half hidden by the depth test. The line then shows thin and broken. With the offset, the line has its full width.** ## Proposed change 1. **Wide lines.** Draw each overlay segment as a quad that faces the screen (two triangles). The vertex shader extends the quad to the line width in pixels. The fragment shader fades the edges for anti-aliasing. - Use one instance for each segment (36 bytes), and make the 6 corners in the shader. Do not write 6 full vertices for each segment. At the overlay limit (`MAX_OVERLAY_VERTICES`, 512k segments), the trial layout used approximately 135 MB. The instanced layout uses approximately 18 MB, which is less than the current 24 MB. - Extend each end by half the line width and fade the end. Then two lines that meet at a corner (for example, a height-plane rectangle) close the corner and do not overlap past it. 2. **Line width setting.** The default is 1.5 pt. The range is approximately 1 to 3 pt. Multiply the value by the pixels-per-point of the display. 3. **Depth offset.** Move each wide-line vertex toward the eye by approximately 3 line widths of world distance. Calculate the world size of one pixel from the `mvp` matrix (the length of its y row), thus the offset is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection. In perspective, the vertex moves along the eye ray, thus the line does not move on the screen. - Effect: a line that is behind a face by less than approximately 3 line widths shows through. This is a few pixels of depth on the screen, which is much less than a real feature. 4. **MSAA setting: Off, 2x, 4x.** The default is 4x. - All viewport pipelines and the trace composite pipeline (`crates/ui/src/trace/composite.rs`) must use the same sample count. The pass renders into a multisampled target and resolves into the current colour texture. - WebGPU guarantees only 1 and 4 samples. 2x needs the device feature `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` and a check of the adapter's sample counts for the colour and depth formats. If the adapter does not support a count, do not show it, or use the nearest supported count and write a log line. - The web build shows Off and 4x only. ## Cost - **MSAA 4x memory.** The colour and depth targets have 4 samples. At 2560×1440, this is approximately 120 MB more GPU memory. At 4K, it is approximately 265 MB. 2x uses half. An integrated GPU is the most sensitive, thus MSAA is a setting. - **MSAA and the traced stock.** The composite writes `frag_depth` once for each pixel. Thus MSAA does not smooth the traced stock edges. Its cost does not change. - **Wide lines.** The overlay uploads only when the scene digest changes (`view_pass::sync_scene`), not when the camera moves. The GPU does approximately 3 times more vertex work and blends approximately 3 to 4 times more line pixels. This is small compared to the model mesh. - Measure the frame time before and after with the `frame_cost` timers, on a large toolpath and on an integrated GPU. Write the readings in the PR. ## Not changed - The geometry, the toolpaths and the posted G-code do not change. This is a display change only. - The pixel goldens (`docs/images/`, `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/`) change at the cut, not in the PR (AGENTS.md "Pixel snapshots are release-lane"). ## Done means - Toolpaths, height planes, region outlines and the other overlay lines draw as anti-aliased lines of the set width. The default is 1.5 pt, multiplied by the pixels-per-point of the display. - A line that lies on a face shows its full width. - The corners of a height-plane rectangle close and do not overlap past the corner. - The MSAA setting (Off / 2x / 4x) and the line width setting persist. An unsupported sample count does not crash and writes a log line. - Tests: - A GPU readback test shows that a line on a face has its full width. - A test shows the instanced buffer size for each segment. - A test shows the fallback of an unsupported sample count. - The PR has the frame-time readings. Proposed labels: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`

body:
Requested by @vilts.

## Goal

Replicate toolpaths that are already calculated, so that the user does not program the same feature many times. There are two methods:

1. **Pattern.** Copy the toolpaths to more positions:
   - **Linear pattern:** copies in one direction (count and spacing).
   - **Grid pattern:** copies in two directions (count and spacing in each direction).
   - **Circular pattern:** copies around a rotary axis (count and angle step). The machine indexes the rotary axis to each copy.
2. **Mirror.** Copy the toolpaths to the other side of a plane that the user selects.

## Proposed structure

- A new **pattern folder** inside a setup. It holds one or more operations of that setup.
- The user sets the pattern or the mirror on the folder. The folder replicates each operation in it.
- A change to an operation in the folder changes all its copies.

## Use cases

- **Plate work:** put one model in a corner of the plate, program it, then replicate it 100 times over the plate.
- **Symmetrical part:** program one half of the part, then mirror the toolpaths to the other half.

## Checks

- **Pattern:** the operations in the folder are checked against the original model. The copies are replicated over the stock. They do not have a model of their own to check against.
- **Mirror:** the mirror is on the same part, so each mirrored toolpath gets the full checks against the model (gouges and the other checks).

## Open questions for research

The requester's suggestions for questions 1-5 are a start point. They are not decisions. The research can change them, and it records the reason for each change.

1. **Folder:** is the folder an operation group in the setup tree? Can a folder hold another folder? Can the user turn off one copy (for example, a position with a clamp)?
   - *Suggestion:* a folder inside the setup, not a separate setup with a different WCS for each copy. All copies use the WCS of the setup. The user can turn off one copy.
2. **Order of the copies:** does the post cut all operations at one copy, then go to the next copy? Or does it cut one operation at each copy, then go to the next operation (fewer tool changes)? Is this a folder setting?
   - *Suggestion:* a folder setting with two values:
     - **By part:** finish one copy completely, then go to the next copy.
     - **By tool:** cut with one tool at each copy, then change to the next tool.
3. **Posted output:** does the post write each copy as expanded moves? Or does it use subprograms (`M98`, `G65`), local coordinate shifts (`G52`) or more work offsets (`G54.1 P..`)? Which of these does each built-in post support?
   - *Suggestion:*
     - Default: one full program with the moves of each copy written out.
     - Option: subprograms.
     - Option: a coordinate shift (`G52`), which makes the program smaller.
     - No work offset for each copy: the number of work offsets limits the number of copies, and a work offset cannot mirror.
4. **Circular pattern:** the request is a pattern around a rotary axis (indexed A or B). Is a circular pattern in the XY plane, around a point, also necessary on a 3-axis machine?
   - *Suggestion:* not necessary on a 3-axis machine.
5. **Mirror and cut direction:** a mirror changes climb milling into conventional milling. It also swaps `G2`/`G3` and the compensation side (`G41`/`G42`). Does the mirror keep the climb direction of the original (the path is reversed), or is this a setting?
   - *Suggestion:* a setting. The default keeps the cut direction that the user set on the operation: a climb cut stays a climb cut.
6. **Checks of the copies:** what is the minimum check for a pattern copy? For example: the copy stays inside the stock, the copy does not hit a fixture or a clamp, and the stock simulation includes all copies. A copy that fails a check must block the post (AGENTS.md "Never Crash, Never Gouge").
7. **Commands:** the folder, the pattern and the mirror need undoable commands and MCP tools (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command").
8. **Relation to nesting:** #2166 copies a part's operations to each nested position on a router sheet. Can the two features use the same transform of a toolpath?

## Related

- #2166 Nesting: copies the operations of a part to each placed position.
- #1720 WCS flip.

## Done means

The open questions above have answers in the comments of this issue. The sub-issues for the work are filed with their priorities and effort labels and linked here. Then this issue closes.

Proposed labels (I cannot set labels): `enhancement`, `needs-research`, `P?`, `effort:max`, `area:post`, `area:multiaxis`, `area:sim`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`.

body:
Found by the read-only review of PR #2918 (comment of 2026-11-20). The finding comes from a read of the code. No run proves it yet.

## What can happen

A STEP file can use the short entity names of ISO 10303-21. The solidcore p21 parser changes some short names to the long names (`SHORT_NAMES`, `solidcore-record/src/step/p21.rs:614-659` at the pinned revision), for example `A2PL3D`, `CRTPNT`, `DRCTN` and `LNGUNT`. It does not change the short forms of `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and `SI_UNIT`.

The unit read of the model import (`length_units` in `camcraft-kernel`, and the units module of solidcore) finds only the long name `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`. Thus a short-name file gives geometry but no unit context. If the reader then uses 1 mm for each unit, a model in inches or metres has the wrong size by a factor of 25.4 or 1000. No refusal or note tells the user.

Wrong geometry is wrong output for each toolpath and each gouge check. Thus the priority is `P1` until a test shows a refusal.

## Where

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs` (`length_units`, near line 244).
- The same defect class in the tool-body read is a blocker of PR #2918 (`crates/geometry/src/step_csys_read.rs:28-30`, `crates/geometry/src/step_units.rs:37-62`). That PR repairs the tool-body read only.

## Not known

- If the reader before PR #2904 (truck-stepio) had the same result for short-name files.
- If a CAD system that our users have writes short names. The form is legal but not common.

## What is expected

- A file that has geometry and a length-unit record, but no unit context that the reader can find, is refused by name. The unit laws of #306 and #689 apply.
- Better: the reader knows the short names of the unit entities and reads the unit.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with short entity names and an inch unit, is in `testdata/models/`.
- A test imports it. The result is the correct size in millimetres, or a refusal that names the missing unit context. The result is never a model at 1 mm for each unit.
- The same test set has a metre file.

Refs #917

body:
The maintainer asked for this on 2026-11-20, after he saw that only one of the three runners works:

> The issue would need to not only split the post work into several "lanes" - it would also need to produce artifacts that gets collected and handed back for inspection. All the lanes could then be queued if we reduce the amount of runner but also run in parallell when we have more runners..

Now: `post-merge.yml` has one job, `gate`. It runs the whole batch tier (about 950 steps) on one runner. The runners `wopr` and `uma` have the label `camcraft-post-merge`. One of them works and the other waits. A run lasts about 40 minutes. The concurrency group `post-merge-main` allows one run at a time. A new push queues behind the running gate or cancels it.

Wanted:
- The batch tier is split into lanes. Each lane is one job of the workflow, for example a matrix over groups of test binaries, clippy, and the build.
- The lanes are independent. With three runners, three lanes run at the same time. With one runner, the lanes queue and give the same result as today.
- Each lane writes its logs and its result to an artifact (`gate-logs/` as `xtask gate` makes them). A final job collects all artifacts. It writes one verdict, with the red steps named, for the rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)`.
- A person or an agent can download the artifact of any lane and read the failure without a second run. The verdict names each lane, its runner, its time and its result.
- The report job (known defect #1611: skipped) is repaired or replaced as part of this work.

Open questions for the work:
- How `cargo xtask gate batch` splits into lanes: by a flag such as `--lane N/M`, or by named groups. The split must be deterministic, and each test binary must run in exactly one lane.
- How lanes share the build. Each runner builds the debug test binaries one time, or one job builds and uploads them. The compile cache (`sccache`) and the size of the artifacts matter here.
- How the lanes treat a push during a run (cancel all lanes, or finish and queue).
- Whether `m3` (macOS, label `camcraft-pr-test`) can join. The label rule in the `runners` skill allows a trigger only on `main` and only for self-hosted runners.

Safety (AGENTS.md "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted"):
- No new `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger. The triggers stay as they are.
- No lane runs code of a fork PR on a self-hosted runner.
- The change touches process files (`xtask/`, the workflow, the `gate` and `runners` skills). The PR body has the line `Process change: yes`. The merging session bumps `PROCESS_VERSION` after the merge.

Done means: one push to `main` runs at least two lanes at the same time when two runners are free. The lanes together run the same test binaries as the batch tier today, with no binary lost. The collector job gives one verdict with the artifacts attached. The `runners` and `gate` skills describe the lanes.

title: Threading: a pass cannot start in front of the end face - the verdict reads free air as rest and blocks the post

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found during the work on #2394 (example case turning/cone-thread).

## What happens

A thread at the free end of a part cannot start in front of the end face. The threading verdict blocks the post.

- The thread kernel puts a V at each lattice point whose band (centre plus and minus half the insert width) overlaps the window (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`, `k_hi`).
- The meridian scan (`crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`, `scan`) judges each interval that a band covers. In front of the end face the model radius is 0. The V floor is capped at the crest radius. The scan reads the difference as rest.

## Steps

1. Model a bar with a 10 mm thread diameter, 0.92 mm deep V grooves each 1.5 mm, and the end face at Z78. The last groove centre is at Z77.5.
2. Add a Threading operation with a 1.2 mm wide, 60 degree insert. Set the window top to Z78 or above.
3. Generate.

Result: `finish envelope near move 64: 0.0000 mm gouge, 5.0000 mm rest`. The post is blocked. The band of the last V (Z76.9 to Z78.1) is 0.1 mm past the end face.

A window top of Z81 gives the same result: lattice points at Z79 and Z80.5 are in free air, and the verdict reads them as 5 mm of rest.

## What is expected

A threading pass can start in free air in front of the end face. This is the usual practice: the pass starts some pitches before the part so that the spindle and the feed are synchronised. Air in front of the end face is not rest.

## Workaround

Put the last groove of the model so that the insert band ends exactly on the end face. Each pass then starts inside the part length with a feed plunge (G32 output). The case of #2394 does this: last centre at Z77.4, band Z76.8 to Z78.0.

This workaround is not safe with the G76 cycle. See the related issue "G76 cycle starts inside the part".

Refs #2394

title: Touching solids: a face bounded only by shared edges, and the feature graph, read the shared edge as non-manifold

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

Since #917, the STEP reader gives each solid of a file its own facets. Two closed solids that touch along a wall can put one mesh edge into 2k facets, k in each direction.

The branch of #917 (PR B, stacked on #2843) adds one rule in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/shared_edge.rs`, `solids_touch`. The slicer (`slice_bodies::closed_solids`) and the winding check (`pick/winding.rs`) use it. The rule passes such an edge when all of these are true:

- the count is even and balanced
- each body uses the edge one time in each direction
- no apex is on the edge line
- each body has a facet on the plane of a facet of a different body

The bodies come from a link over plain edges only (two uses, one in each direction).

The rule fixes the shipped `sample_ap214.step`: it slices, and it reads as outward for Align. Two cases stay open:

1. **A face whose full boundary is shared edges.** Example: two blocks stacked face to face. The contact face of each block links to no other facet of its block over a plain edge. Thus each shared edge sees four bodies that use it one time each, and the rule refuses. Align then refuses the model as non-manifold. The slicer refuses it by name.
2. **The feature graph** (`geometry::feature::features_of_facets`) has its own edge map. It does not use the rule. On `sample_ap214.step`, 216 tangent edge pieces pick apart (`no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture`).

## Rules that were tried

- **Radial pairing** (pair each facet with its angular neighbour about the edge). It failed on the sample: the solids overlap, and two facets in the same direction lie on one plane, so the order is ambiguous. It also let two cubes that meet only along one line pass, which is wrong.
- **Wall on a wall** (`solids_touch`, kept). It fails in case 1, because the bodies form before the shared edges are judged.

## Safety

Neither case gives wrong toolpath output. Each is a refusal by name, or an edge that picks in pieces. The pins:

- `shared_face_bodies::welded_non_manifold_solids_are_refused_as_a_model_fault`
- `shared_face_bodies::the_sample_laid_flat_generates_3d_finish_and_pocket_with_no_gouge`

## Wanted

- Link a face that only shared edges bound to its own solid. For example, use the STEP solid ranges (`Mesh::solid_ranges`, `app::mesh_solids`) when the model has them, or pair the coplanar opposed facets first.
- Give the feature graph the same rule.
- Remove the known-fail markers that name this issue.

body:
Found by the new Windows check (Windows 11, Git for Windows defaults: `core.autocrlf=true`), main 380c29b3c, `cargo xtask gate quick`.

## What happens

Git for Windows checks text files out with CRLF by default. `.gitattributes` pins `crates/app/tests/golden/**`, tester kits, examples and `*.sh` to LF, but not every fixture that tests compare byte for byte or parse. Four suites (17 tests) fail on such a checkout, each within a second:

| Suite | Reads | Pinned? |
|---|---|---|
| post `explain_fanuc_family`, `explain_remaining` | `crates/post/tests/golden/explain/*.nc` | **no** |
| app `wire_taper_angle` | `crates/app/tests/edm/wire-iso-fixture.mch` (include_str) | **no** |
| app `import_step_curve_guard` | `testdata/models/box.step` (include_str) | **no** |

Example: `fanuc_explain_golden_preserves_program` - left (generated) ends lines with `\n`, right (golden from the checkout) with `\r\n`; the content is otherwise identical.

## Fix

Pin every byte-compared or parsed text fixture to LF, e.g.:

```
crates/*/tests/golden/** text eol=lf
crates/*/tests/**/*.mch  text eol=lf
testdata/**/*.step       text eol=lf
testdata/**/*.stp        text eol=lf
```

(or one broader rule for `crates/*/tests/**` and `testdata/**`), then `git add --renormalize .`. A unit test in xtask (or a CI-free check) could assert that `git check-attr eol` is `lf` for every file under the golden/fixture dirs.

## Done means

On a fresh Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`, the four suites above pass; `git check-attr eol -- <each fixture>` reports `lf`.

```rust
drop(point);
```

`point` is a closure that borrows `ent` mutably. The closure has no `Drop` implementation, so `drop(point)` does nothing. The borrow ends at the last call of the closure.

With `-D warnings`, the clippy step of the gate is red on this toolchain.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install the stable toolchain with clippy 0.1.98.
2. Run `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`.
3. Clippy gives `error: call to std::mem::drop with a value that does not implement Drop`.

## Fix

Remove the line `drop(point);`. The test does not change its behaviour.

The rotary operations (Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) show the same Heights page as the 3-axis operations: Clearance, Retract, Top and Bottom as Z values in the setup frame (the viewport labels them, e.g. "Clearance 3.6733 (stock top +0.9843)"). A rotary operation shows the four heights as radii, the generated path keeps them (pinned by a test that measures the tool tip's distance from the axis on every link and rapid), the viewport draws them about the axis, and a radius inside the stock is refused by name.

body: ### What are you trying to do I want to describe my own machine in the Machines pane, for example a 3-axis grblHAL mill with a 4th-axis rotary (A, about X) on the table. The file editor (machine_file_editor.rs) shows one field for each key the file already has (machine::fields). It cannot add an axis, remove one or change their order in kinematics.default.parts. Today I have to edit the .mch file in a text editor and reload it. ### How you imagine it working - One row per axis part, in chain order, under `table` or under `head` in `kinematics.default.parts`, with up, down and remove buttons and an "add axis" control. A linear part is `X`, `Y`, `Z` (and `U`, `V` for a wire machine); a rotary part is `A`, `B` or `C`. - A linear row edits `direction` (`1` / `-1`, #373). - A rotary row edits `axis` (±X, ±Y, ±Z, or three numbers for any other vector) and its travel, or none for continuous. - A rotary that turns the work also edits `nose_to_axis` and `axis_to_table` (#785), the two distances the clearance gates read. They are measurable with a rule or taken from the maker's data. - Under them, a collapsed "Kinematics" group holds `pivot` and `offset` (#1962). It is closed by default and open when the file already states a pivot. For a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head), the group is open instead, since the two distances do not apply to it and the pivot is what places it. This issue only adds the group; #1970's rows fill it (see below). - The letter follows the `axis` by RS-274: about X is `A`, about Y is `B`, about Z is `C`. When `axis` is set, the editor suggests that letter. A row whose letter and `axis` disagree (an `A` about Y, say) shows a note at the row; whether that should also block a save is the validator's call, as now. - The edits go through `MachineDraft`, as `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant` do, so keys the editor does not know are kept. - The validator judges the result as now. A refusal shows at the row it concerns, and a save stays blocked while a refusal stands. - Moving a rotary changes its `parent` and `chain_order`, since the parser derives them from the nesting (#1962). Tests pin that, and that `pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover` and `sign_convention` survive an add, a move and a remove. For illustration only, the axis list as it started to look in another CAM tool (solidcraft). It is a hint at the idea, not a layout to copy. Its `Pivot` row stands in the open; the proposal here puts the pivot in a collapsed group instead. **Overlap with #1970.** #1970 adds rows for the #1962 trunnion keys to `fields.rs` and `sheet.rs`, the same files and the same rotary row. This issue does not edit those keys; it only keeps them, and the rotary row's collapsed "Kinematics" group is where #1970's rows go. Its blockers (#1962, #1965, #1968) look done on `main`, so the two may run at the same time. Should this one wait for #1970, go first, or be folded into it? **A question before any code.** A rotary can be placed by `nose_to_axis` / `axis_to_table` (#785) or by `pivot` / `offset` (#1962). I do not see them as alternatives: the clearance gates read the #785 pair, the post's kinematics the #1962 pair, so a file may well want both. Hence the proposal above rather than a choice between them: a rotary that turns the work shows the two distances, with `pivot` / `offset` in a collapsed group; a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head) shows the group open, since the two distances do not apply to it. Does that split work for you, or should the editor show both pairs alike? **And one about a machine with both.** `nose_to_axis` is measured with Z at `safe_retract`, and as I read it with the head straight. On a machine with a tilting head (B under `head`) and a rotary that turns the work (A under `table`), the nose moves away from that line as B tilts, so the one number no longer holds. Do the index-swing gates handle such a machine today? If not, should the editor still offer the two distances on its A, or say that they are judged only with the head straight? I would like to take this one if it is wanted.

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> when hitting simulation there sh ould be an option to "step" thru to next operation.. so we can check the one relevant

## Problem

The simulation plays the whole program from the first move. A user who wants to check one operation must scrub or wait. There is no way to go to the next operation.

## Wanted

1. The simulation controls have a "next operation" step. It moves the playback position to the first move of the next operation in program order.
2. A matching "previous operation" step. It moves to the start of the current operation, and a second press moves to the start of the one before it.
3. The control shows which operation is current (its name from the tree). A step across a setup boundary, a tool change or a WCS change works the same as a step inside one setup.
4. The stock shown at the new position is correct: it is the stock after all earlier operations. A step must give the same stock as playback to that position. A step never skips a removal.
5. Disabled states: "next" is disabled in the last operation. "previous" is disabled at the start of the first operation. The AccessKit labels and the tooltips say what each button does.
6. A keyboard shortcut for each step, listed in the shortcut help.

## Notes

- The playback position is ephemeral UI state (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command"), so no undoable command is needed. If a step selects an operation in the tree, that selection goes through `SelectEntity`.
- A skipped or suppressed operation is not a stop. An operation with no toolpath is not a stop.
- UI text: plain English, no G-code jargon. A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, enabled state and the position, not pixel values (`crates/ui/AGENTS.md`).
- Related: #2587 (the stand-alone simulator window). The same step logic should work there. Keep the operation-boundary lookup in the lowest crate that provides it, so both can use it.

## Done means

- A test shows that "next" from a position inside operation 1 gives the first move of operation 2, and that the stock equals the stock from plain playback to that move.
- Tests for the first operation, the last operation, a tool change and an operation with no toolpath.
- The behaviour tests and the page layout test of the simulation panel pass.

body:
## Request

Add a post for classic Grbl 1.1 (3-axis mill). Many small routers and hobby mills run Grbl 1.1 on an Arduino-class board. The `grblHAL` post (#710) writes words that Grbl 1.1 refuses, so it is not a replacement.

## Differences to the grblHAL post

From the public Grbl 1.1 documentation (the "Commands" and "Interface" wiki pages, behaviour only):

- No canned cycles. Grbl 1.1 has `G80` but not `G73`, `G81`-`G89`. The post must expand drill, peck and bore cycles to `G0` / `G1` / `G4` moves.
- No `M6`. A tool change is `M5`, a retract to a safe Z in machine coordinates (`G53 G0 Z...`), then `M0` with a comment that names the tool. `T` is written in a comment only.
- No `G43 H`. The length offset is `G43.1 Z...` or nothing. Default: write no length offset (the user zeroes each tool), and write `G49` in the preamble.
- No `O` program number. No `G41` / `G42`. No `G98` / `G99`.
- `G4 P` is in seconds.
- Line buffer of 80 characters: keep each block short. Comments are `( )` only. Do not write comments with nested brackets.
- Coolant: `M7`, `M8`, `M9` only. Other coolant kinds are refused by name.

## Acceptance

- A built-in post `Grbl 1.1` and a machine file `grbl-3axis.mch`.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill (expanded), peck (expanded), bore with dwell, two tools.
- A test that each posted line is 80 characters or less, and that no unsupported word (`G8x`, `M6`, `G43 H`, `G41`, `G42`, `O`) is posted.

I can do this work in a PR from my fork.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0. His words:

> The tool editor page needs a re work, Input fields sitting left of the input, cutting data by material should be default behavior and the default "value" is what we have in the catalog now. We can have a material called "Unknown" that is the default value.  Why there is two previews of the tool is also strange. One drawn profile of the tool and the holder picked should be enough. The holder library, should remove the parametric holder values and "fill them in" with the values from the library.. There is no need for having a Weldon for each "sized tool".. a weldon is a weldon, and whatever tool will fit it.
> In general the Tool editor needs a complete overhaul.

This is an umbrella issue. Research it, then file one sub-issue for each part, and close this issue.

## Parts

1. **Layout.** Put each label on the left of its input field, in a property grid (see the Fusion-style dialog rule: collapsible groups, tooltips).
2. **Cutting data by material is the default.** Each tool has cutting data (speed, feed, stepdown, stepover) for each material. The current single set of values becomes the data of a material named `Unknown`. `Unknown` is the default material. Existing tool libraries and project files load with their values moved to `Unknown`, with no loss.
3. **One preview.** The editor shows one drawing: the tool profile and the holder that the user selected. Remove the second preview. (See #2005: the body and the spun profile draw over each other.)
4. **Holders come from the holder library.** The user selects a holder from the library. The holder values (diameter, length, gauge length) come from the library entry and are not typed into each tool. Remove the parametric holder fields from the tool.
5. **A holder is not sized to a tool.** One holder entry (for example a Weldon holder) serves each tool whose shank fits it. Do not keep one holder entry for each tool size. The fit check (shank diameter against the holder bore) must give a clear refusal when a tool does not fit.

## Questions for the research

- The tool library and project file format change (parts 2, 4, 5). Give the migration and the version bump. This can be a breaking change.
- How the collision check and the simulation get the holder shape after part 4. They must use the same shape that the preview shows.
- Where cutting data by material connects to the operation: the operation uses the material of the setup stock, or `Unknown` when the stock has no material.

body:
**The request (mkinney, 2026-11-15):** "Do we need to handle svg file import?" ... "Yes file it". Many waterjet, laser and plasma users draw in Inkscape or Illustrator and export SVG. WAZER's own app takes SVG and DXF (see #1525).

## What

Import an SVG file as 2D sketch geometry for 2D operations (Contour, Pocket, Engrave/Trace, plasma or waterjet profile). It goes into the same sketch entity as the DXF import, so the operations need no new input path.

## Depends on

- #1860 (DXF core reader), #1861 (2D sketch chaining, outer-vs-hole nesting, open chains) and #1862 (the sketch ECS entity, .camproj persistence, undoable import).
- Stack on those: the SVG reader only produces sketch chains and reuses chaining, nesting and the import command.

## Scope

- **Elements:** `path` (M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`. `g` groups with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skew), applied to the geometry.
- **Curves:** cubic and quadratic Béziers and elliptical arcs become arcs or polylines within the document's chord tolerance. An arc stays an arc where it is circular after the transform.
- **Units and scale:** `width`/`height` with units (mm, cm, in, pt, pc, px), and the `viewBox`. px uses 96 px/in (the CSS rule). If the file states no physical size, the import asks for the scale. It never guesses silently.
- **Y axis:** SVG Y points down. Flip it so the drawing appears as it does in the editor.
- **Ignored, with a note:** fill, stroke style, text (unless converted to paths), images, clip paths, masks, `use` references to symbols outside the file.
- **Refusals, by name:** a malformed path, a zero or negative size, a degenerate arc, and a file larger than the import budget give a clear error, never a panic (the Prime Directive).
- **MCP:** an `import_svg` tool, or the shared sketch-import tool with format svg (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool").

## Not in scope (later)

- Text to outlines (fonts), embedded images, and CSS stylesheets.

## Done means

- A fixture SVG set (a rectangle with a hole, Bézier and arc shapes, a nested group with transforms, mm and in documents, and one file without a physical size) imports to the expected sketch chains. The tests pin the chain count, closure, nesting and size within tolerance.
- A 2D Contour on an imported SVG posts. A golden is pinned for one plasma or waterjet-style profile.
- Malformed fixtures are refused by name and never panic. The importer fuzz test covers the SVG reader.
- The user guide import page (and #1525's waterjet notes) lists SVG.

Related: #1525 (waterjet research), #1452 (DXF umbrella), #1860-#1870 (DXF chain).

body:
What happens: post-merge run 43535610115 (push to main at 745edc36a) ended with job `gate` = failure and job `report` = skipped. The rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)` was not opened or commented on.

Expected: AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background": a red post-merge gate opens or comments on the rolling issue; the next green run closes it.

Cause (read from `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` on main): the `report` job has `needs: gate` and an `if:` with no status-check function:

```
if: ${{ (needs.gate.result == 'success' || needs.gate.result == 'failure') && needs.gate.outputs.skipped != 'true' && (...) }}
```

GitHub Actions adds an implicit `success()` to a job's `if` unless it contains `always()`, `failure()`, `cancelled()` or `!cancelled()`. With a failed `needs` job the implicit `success()` is false, so the job is skipped before the expression is read. The job therefore only ever runs on green.

Suggested fix: start the condition with `always() &&` (the rest already excludes cancelled and skipped runs). One line.

Note on this particular run: its only red test was `a_lowered_cap_refuses_the_same_face_at_once` (`crates/app/tests/import_step_guard.rs`, "not within 30s"), the wall-clock flake of issue 1605, so main was not truly red here. The reporting gap is real for any failure.

A `.github/` change: the PR is read, not built, and waits for the maintainer (`needs-maintainer`). `Process change: yes` does not apply (`.github/` is not a process file).

Found by the maintenance session while watching runs.

Done means: a post-merge run whose gate fails runs `report` and opens or comments on the rolling issue; a green run after it closes that issue; a cancelled or cut-skipped run still reports nothing.

- **Used:** WAZER's public documentation (its support article on G-code and its materials and specs page; URLs below, cited, not copied), the Pro WAZER user manual (behaviour only), general abrasive-waterjet knowledge, and a behavioural analysis of the user's own job files exported by WAZER's web app (WAM). Those are about 120 programs from WAM 1.6 to 2.4, all Pro WAZER. Only their word and code usage and statistics were studied; no file is shared or committed.
- **Not used, and never to be used:** any Autodesk Fusion or HSMWorks post or output for WAZER (one exists in Autodesk's post library; it was not opened), WAM's JavaScript, and the machine's firmware.
- **Licence:** WAZER's G-code page is proprietary ("all rights reserved"). It is a published description of the dialect, not an open specification. Facts such as code numbers and meanings may be implemented; its text may not be copied.

## Findings so far

**Dialect** (WAM output, meanings as WAZER publishes them):
- **Modes:** G21 (mm) and G90 only. Moves are G0 and G1 only: **no arcs**, so curves are short segments. **No Z axis.** F is in mm/min. Dwell is `G4 S<seconds>`.
- **Jet and abrasive:** M3/M5 open and close the water, M8/M9 the abrasive.
- **Machine-specific M codes:** start and end of job (no M2/M30), the cut's bounding box (used by the machine's "check cut extents"), re-pierce time after a pause, and header metadata (WAM version, material name truncated to 20 characters, thickness, estimated time).
- **File format:** CRLF line endings, `;` comments, a fixed parameter header.
- **Origin:** top-left of the bed, Y negative toward the front. The cutting area is about 460 × 305 mm.
- **Per contour:** rapid to the pierce point, water on, abrasive on, stationary pierce dwell, straight lead-in, contour, then a short dwell, abrasive off, dwell, water off, dwell. The jet is never on during a rapid.
- **Kerf:** compensation is in the geometry (about half the published kerf), with no G41/G42.
- **Tabs** are uncut gaps (most contours are open).
- **Cut order:** inner contours first.
- **Feed:** the file's top F is the material rate for the chosen quality. The three qualities run at about 1 : 1.14 : 1.29. **Corner slowdown is written into F** in steps, down to about 0.45×.

**Machine:** kerf about 1.1 mm (0.044 in), maximum about 75 ipm; the pressure differs between the Pro and desktop models. The manual's error list includes a refusal of files generated by a much older WAM than the firmware.

**Materials and speeds:** the public page gives, per material and thickness, a cut rate and pierce time for each of the Pro and desktop machines. The published Pro rates sit near WAM's fine-to-medium rates; WAM's pierce times are often shorter than the published ones.

**Warranty and terms:** WAZER states that only WAM-generated files are approved, and that **edited or third-party-generated files void the warranty and breach its terms of service.** A community report says non-WAM files can leave uncut sections after pause and resume. Any CamCraft WAZER post must carry this warning prominently and must not claim WAZER approval.

## Open questions (answer before any sub-issue)

1. **Should CamCraft ship a WAZER post at all,** given the warranty and terms-of-service statement, or only a generic abrasive-waterjet post plus a user-supplied machine file? Decide with the maintainer.
2. **Pause and resume:** what does the firmware need for a third-party program to resume correctly (re-pierce after a pause, the bounding-box words)? Can that be learned from public docs alone?
3. **The corner-slowdown model:** derive it from public waterjet literature (taper and lag versus speed) rather than copying WAM's step table. What do the references say?
4. **Pierce data:** reuse #1521 (pierce and dwell data keyed by material and thickness), with waterjet as a process kind there?
5. **The operation:** a 2D abrasive-waterjet profile op, or a waterjet mode of the existing plasma/laser profile? Covers kerf offset in the geometry, leads on open contours, tabs as gaps, inner contours first, and arc linearisation tolerance.
6. **The machine file:** bed envelope and origin, kerf, max feed, model-specific speed tables (Pro vs desktop) and the bounding-box limit check.
7. **WAM project files (`.wzr`):** these are JSON with the source drawing and settings, undocumented. Importing them is out of scope unless WAZER documents the format; record that decision.

## Candidate sub-issues (filed only after the questions above are answered)

- Abrasive-waterjet profile operation (kerf, leads, tabs as gaps, inner-first order)
- Waterjet corner-slowdown and pierce-time model from published literature
- WAZER (Pro and desktop) machine definition and post, from the public dialect, with the warranty warning
- Waterjet process data in #1521's pierce and dwell tables

## Public references

- WAZER, "Understanding G-code": https://support.wazer.com/resources/preprocessing-temp/understanding-g-code
- WAZER materials and specs: https://wazer.com/materials/materials-specs/
- WAZER web app (WAM): https://wam.wazer.com/wazercam (a JavaScript app; no format docs without logging in)

Related: #1521 (plasma, laser and waterjet pierce and dwell data).

Done means: each open question is answered in a comment, the sub-issues are filed (one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, a Done means line and "Part of #<this>"), and this umbrella is closed with links to them.

body:
> bug; tools like plasma cutter - or laser for that matter, and prob waterjet as well. Would require piercing and dwell data.. Lasers usually have 1-4 piercing steps that can be used all or just one. just to get thru different thickness of material. Same with plasma.. piercing height, power at height, pressure of gas, movement of torch/laser head etc etc. Use perplexit to research this in a subagent and make a issue ticket from it where this types of tools getter better coverage.

(Maintainer, 2026-11-13, in chat.)

## What exists today

- Plasma only. `ToolKind::Torch` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs`) is a kerf width plus rpm 0; it carries no cutting data. I found no laser or waterjet tool kind in `tools.rs`.
- The plasma operation (`crates/motion/src/plasma/mod.rs`, `emit.rs`; app side `crates/app/src/operation/types/plasma.rs`, `crates/app/src/project/plasma_dto.rs`; page `crates/ui/src/egui_app/plasma_page.rs`) has three optional per-operation numbers: pierce height, cut height, pierce delay. Left empty means "set by the controller" (AutoFS).
- The Tormach plasma post (`assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`) writes M207/M208/M209 for those three values and G16 for the pierce, and leaves volts, amps and gas to the control's own table. Nothing else (power, gas, pressure, torch motion at the pierce) can be stated anywhere.
- Related open issues: 621 (plasma research umbrella), 1447 (common-line cutting and marking), 1452 (DXF import for 2D cuts). No open issue covers pierce data; a "pierce" search finds only closed plasma work (670, 671).

## What is missing

1. Cut data lives on the operation, not on the tool, and is not keyed by material or thickness. Changing plate thickness means re-typing numbers.
2. Only one pierce, with one height and one delay. No transfer height, no puddle-jump (lift after pierce), no creep or start-speed ramp on exit, no amperage or gas on the tool.
3. Laser and waterjet have no tool kind, so there is nowhere to put multi-stage pierce data.
4. Posts have no way to say "this stage cannot be written in this dialect".

## Research summary (facts and concepts only, own words)

Plasma
- Transfer height: the low height where the arc first transfers to the plate. Pierce height: the higher height held while the arc pierces (limits spray onto the torch). Pierce delay: time held after transfer before the head moves. Cut height: stand-off while cutting. Torch height control holds a target arc voltage as a stand-in for the distance during the cut.
- Puddle jump (optional): after the pierce, lift to a percentage of pierce height for a short dwell to clear molten metal, then drop to cut height.
- Each system and consumable set has a maximum pierce thickness; thicker plate needs an edge start (the arc begins off the plate edge). Kerf comes from the cut chart.
- The maker's cut chart is the source of values (current, gas type and pressure, heights, voltage, speed). It normally sits in the control's material table; the program selects it and may override single values.

Laser
- Makers document up to four sequential pierce stages, each with its own time, power, pulse frequency, duty cycle, focus, nozzle distance, gas type and pressure; a stage with zero time is skipped. Parameters may ramp from a start to an end value inside a stage.
- Pierce kinds named by makers: ramped, pulsed (gradual), and a forceful short pierce; definitions vary by machine, so the data model must not hard-code them.
- Cooling dwell or gas blow is machine-specific; no standard length exists.
- Normal practice: the technology table (material and thickness) holds the recipe, the NC program selects the table and pierce type and may override.

Waterjet
- Methods: stationary, dynamic (moving toward the path while piercing), wiggle or circular (short oscillation), and low-pressure or pressure-ramp pierce for brittle or laminated material (glass, stone, ceramic, composites). Abrasive can be delayed after water starts, or fed first with pressure ramped up from low.
- No universal pierce time by thickness exists; it depends on material, pressure, nozzle and method, so it must be the user's value.

Control table versus program: recipes are usually in the control's table (selected by material and thickness) with the program choosing and sometimes overriding. A CAM system therefore needs both: store the recipe, then either post the selector or post explicit values, by dialect.

## Proposed data model

A cut-data record per tool, keyed by material and thickness (rows the user adds, copies and deletes):

- Cut parameters: cut height, feed, kerf; for plasma amperage, gas type and pressure, arc voltage; for laser power, frequency, duty, gas type and pressure, nozzle distance, focus; for waterjet pressure and abrasive flow.
- Pierce: an ordered list of 0 to 4 stages, every stage optional and individually enableable. Each stage has height, duration (dwell), power or pressure, frequency and duty (laser), gas and pressure, an optional ramp end value, and head motion during the pierce (none, wiggle or circular amplitude, or moving toward the path). Plasma uses one stage plus optional transfer height and puddle-jump (percent and dwell). Waterjet adds method, low-pressure value and abrasive delay.
- Pierce capacity per record: maximum pierceable thickness, and whether an edge start is allowed.
- Every number is entered by the user or copied from the maker's chart. Shipped example rows are marked "example" in the file and in the UI.

Editing: a cut-data table on the tool page (undoable commands, an MCP tool and script verb per the command law). The operation chooses a row (or "none: the machine's own table") and may override single values; overrides are commands too.

Operation behaviour: pierce at the start of the lead-in, run the stages in order (height move, dwell and head motion per stage), then the cut-height move and lead-in. The generated path carries the stages as records in the CL file so the post and the verifier read the same data.

Posts: each dialect writes the stages it can (dwell, height moves, selector codes or direct values). A stage or value the dialect cannot express makes the post refuse with a named reason, or write a visible comment line naming what was left to the control; it is never dropped silently. The Tormach post keeps M207/M208/M209 for the plasma values and refuses a multi-stage laser record.

## Safety rules

- A thickness above the tool's pierce capacity is refused, unless the operation states an edge start (then the lead-in must start off the plate, and that is verified).
- No silent default for a pierce time or height: an empty value either posts "controller's table" as an explicit, commented choice on a dialect that has one, or refuses.
- Stage values are checked at command creation (non-negative times and heights, power within 0 to 100 percent, at most four stages).
- Values are the user's and the machine maker's; shipped examples are labelled as examples and nothing was run on a real machine. Verification (stage order, pierce inside a kept part, head motion hitting a neighbour) joins the existing plasma laws.
- This changes posted output, so it is at least effort:high.

## Suggested slices

1. Tool-side cut-data record for the existing plasma torch (material and thickness rows, transfer height, puddle jump, pierce capacity), project file round-trip, undoable commands, MCP tool. The operation picks a row.
2. Plasma generation and the Tormach post use the row; refusal for thickness above capacity and the edge-start rule; laws and goldens.
3. Laser tool kind and machine kind with 1 to 4 pierce stages; CL records and a first laser post (dwell and height moves, explicit comment lines).
4. Waterjet tool kind: pierce methods, low-pressure pierce, abrasive delay; post support.
5. Docs and shipped example rows.

Slices 3 and 4 may need their own research issues for machine kinds; file them when slice 1 lands.

Done means: a plasma, laser or waterjet tool carries material and thickness keyed cut data with up to four ordered optional pierce stages; the operation uses the chosen row at the lead-in start; each post writes every stage or refuses or comments what it cannot; a too-thick plate without an edge start is refused; tests pin all of these.

Related: 621, 1447, 1452, 670, 671.

## Sources

- https://linuxcnc.org/docs/master/html/en/plasma/qtplasmac.html
- https://linuxcnc.org/docs/html/plasma/plasma-cnc-primer.html
- https://xnet.hypertherm.com/Xnet/library/download/?file=HYP104561
- https://www.hypertherm.com/resources/more-resources/articles/thick-metal-cutting-techniques/
- https://www.hypertherm.com/resources/more-resources/articles/torch-height-control-for-plasma-cutting/
- https://studylib.net/doc/25809509/amada-cnc-laser-machine-program-manual--2-
- https://www.fanuc.co.jp/en/product/catalog/pdf/cnc/FS30i-LB_0i-LFPlus(E)-03.pdf
- http://www.apasi.net/system/files/9999/2014/P338EN.pdf
- https://pdfcoffee.com/1-user-manual-hd-f-hd-fl-pdf-free.html
- https://www.omax.com/news/blog/4-piercing-methods-abrasive-waterjet-machining
- https://www.aquajet.co.uk/4-piercing-methods/
- https://digitallibrarynasampe.org/data/pdfs/s2019_pdfs/TP19--1458.pdf
- https://patents.google.com/patent/US9108297B2/en

body:
Part of #1445.

The first slice of #1445 (the ream, G85) left fine boring out on purpose. A fine-boring cycle stops the spindle at a fixed orientation at the bottom, shifts the tip away from the wall, then rapids out. The shift direction and amount depend on how the boring bar is clamped relative to the spindle's orientation angle. A guessed default could drag the tip across the finished bore, so no default is posted.

What is owed:
- A drill-op cycle choice for fine boring, with two required user parameters: the shift direction (or angle) and the shift amount, validated at command creation (finite, positive amount, smaller than the hole radius minus the tool's tip extent).
- A machine capability for oriented spindle stop; a machine or post without it refuses the cycle by name, never posts a plain bore in its place.
- Posts that have the canned word write it, with the shift words in that control's own form; the others refuse by name (an expanded chain needs M19-style orientation, which is per control).
- The CL chain the verifier and simulation read: feed in, (dwell), shift, rapid out, so the rapid out is judged against the wall at the shifted position.
- MCP `edit_operation` parameters for both values, a UI row in plain English.

Sources: public controller documentation only (RS-274/NGC, LinuxCNC; vendor programming manuals for the word layout). RS-274/NGC uses G76 for lathe threading; the fine-boring word differs by control and must be read from each post, not assumed.

Done means: fine boring is a user choice that posts only with an orientation-capable machine and an explicit shift, is refused by name otherwise, and is pinned by per-post goldens and a verifier test of the shifted retract.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: hole making has drilling and tapping cycles only. There is no reaming, boring, fine boring or dwell-at-depth cycle, and no spot-face / counterbore dwell. The tool kinds (reamer, spot drill, countersink, centre drill) are open issue 897; this issue is the cycles and their posted output.

Wanted, as cycle choices on the drilling operation (a user parameter with a default, never hard-wired):
- Reaming: feed in, feed out (G85 where the post has it, expanded moves otherwise).
- Boring: feed in, spindle stop, rapid out (G86); feed in, dwell, feed out (G89).
- Fine boring: feed in, oriented spindle stop, shift off the wall, rapid out (G76 on a mill), with the shift amount and direction as parameters. A post or machine with no spindle orientation refuses it by name rather than posting a retract that drags the tip up the wall.
- Dwell at depth for spot facing and counterboring (G82), in the unit each post expects.

Safety: every post either writes the cycle correctly for its dialect, expands it to plain moves, or refuses by name. A dwell is never silently dropped or written in the wrong unit (seconds against milliseconds). The canned cycle and its expanded form remove the same stock in simulation.

Sources: RS-274 / ISO 6983 and each control maker's published programming manual for the cycle words, found by a literature search (Perplexity) at the start of the work and cited in the PR. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: each cycle generates, simulates and posts on Fanuc, Haas, Heidenhain, Sinumerik, grblHAL and PathPilot as a canned cycle, an expansion or a named refusal, pinned by a golden per post; an MCP parameter for the cycle choice; a fine bore on a machine without spindle orientation is refused in a test. Not exercised on real controls unless the PR says otherwise.

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
